title: Cut and form sheet metal to specifications

lessons.title: Reading the job and marking out
lessons.html:
Sheet metal on the farm

On a farm you make and repair many things from sheet metal: guards for belts and PTO shafts, covers, feed troughs, hopper sides, brackets and flashing for sheds. The work must match the specification. The specification tells you:

  • the type of metal, for example mild steel, galvanised steel or aluminium;
  • the thickness, in millimetres;
  • the sizes, shown on a drawing or sketch;
  • where the bends go and the angle of each bend.

Measuring and marking out

  1. Check the drawing. If a size is missing or unclear, ask your supervisor before you cut.
  2. Check the sheet is flat, clean and the right thickness. Use a vernier or a gauge.
  3. Use a steel rule or tape, a square and a scriber to mark lines. A scriber line is thin and exact.
  4. Mark bend lines and holes. Use a centre punch to mark the middle of each hole.
  5. Check all your sizes again before you cut. Measure twice, cut once.

Plan the cuts so you waste as little metal as possible. Sheet metal costs money – a full sheet of galvanised steel can cost hundreds of rand.

Safety

  • Sheet metal edges are as sharp as a knife. Always wear leather gloves when you handle it.
  • Wear safety glasses, safety boots and hearing protection when cutting.
  • Carry large sheets with two people.

lessons.title: Cutting sheet metal
lessons.html:
Choosing the cutting tool

ToolUse
Tin snips (straight, left, right)Thin sheet, short straight cuts and curves
GuillotineLong straight cuts on thicker sheet
NibblerCurves and cut-outs without bending the sheet
Angle grinder with cutting discThicker sheet, when no other tool is available
Drill and hole sawRound holes

Cutting well

  • Cut on the waste side of the line, so the part stays the right size.
  • Clamp the sheet so it does not move.
  • With snips, do not close the blades fully at the end of each cut; this stops a jagged edge.
  • After cutting, remove sharp edges (burrs) with a file or deburring tool.

Angle grinder safety

  • Use the right disc for the grinder speed and for metal. Never use a cracked disc.
  • Keep the guard on. Never take it off.
  • Hold the grinder with both hands.
  • Sparks can start a fire. Clear away dry grass, rags and fuel. Have a fire extinguisher close.
  • Wear a face shield, safety glasses and hearing protection.
  • Unplug the grinder before changing the disc.

Never use a guillotine with your fingers near the blade, and never let another person work the pedal while your hands are in the machine.

lessons.title: Forming, bending and checking
lessons.html:
Bending the metal

Forming means giving the flat metal its shape. Use:

  • a bending brake (folder) for straight bends;
  • a vice with bending bars and a soft hammer for small parts;
  • rollers for curves, like a round trough.
  1. Line the bend line up with the edge of the brake or bending bar.
  2. Clamp firmly.
  3. Bend slowly to the angle on the drawing. Metal springs back a little, so bend slightly past the angle if needed.
  4. Check the angle with a protractor or angle gauge.

Do the bends in the right order. If you bend in the wrong order, you may not be able to fit the next bend in the machine.

Avoiding cracks

A bend that is too sharp can crack, especially on thicker or harder metal. Do not bend the same place back and forth – it makes the metal weak.

Checking against the specification

  • Measure all sizes and compare them with the drawing.
  • Check angles and that the part is square.
  • Check there are no cracks, dents or sharp burrs.
  • Test fit the part on the machine if possible.

Clean up the off-cuts. Sharp scraps on the floor cut boots and tyres. Put them in the scrap bin.

Key points

  • Follow the drawing for metal type, thickness, sizes and bends.
  • Measure twice and cut on the waste side of the line.
  • Always wear gloves; sheet edges are very sharp.
  • Keep the grinder guard on and clear fire risks before cutting.
  • Check the finished part against the specification.
